operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email format and check uniqueness against discussion_board_users.email (unique constraint). 2) Validate password meets security requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one number, one special character. 3) Hash password using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds. 4) Generate new UUID for user id. 5) Create citizen record for sequential ID via discussion_board_user_citizens. 6) Insert new user record with permission_level='MEMBER', is_banned=false, display_name from request. 7) Create new session record in discussion_board_user_sessions with access_token (15min expiry), refresh_token (7day expiry), and connection metadata. 8) Return tokens and user profile in IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Registers a new user account on the Economic/Political Discussion Board platform.

The join operation creates a new user account with email and password authentication. The email must be unique across all users in the discussion_board_users table. The password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, at least one number, and at least one special character. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage in the password_hash field.

Upon successful registration, the user is assigned MEMBER permission_level, which grants access to create articles, write comments, and manage their own content. A display_name is required and will be shown publicly alongside the user's content and on their profile.

The response includes a JWT access token (valid for 15 minutes) and a refresh token (valid for 7 days), enabling immediate authenticated access without requiring a separate login. The access token contains the user's id, email, and permission_level claims for authorization checks on subsequent API calls.

This is a public endpoint requiring no prior authentication. After registration, users can immediately access all member-level features including article creation, commenting, and profile management.

requestBody.description: User registration information including email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user profile information for the newly registered user.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Validate email and password are provided in request body. 2) Query discussion_board_users by email (unique index lookup). 3) If user not found, return AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS error. 4) Check is_banned field - if true, return AUTH_USER_BANNED error with ban reason. 5) Verify password_hash using bcrypt.compare with provided password. 6) If password mismatch, return AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS error (do not reveal which field is wrong). 7) Create new session record in discussion_board_user_sessions with: access_token (JWT with sub=userId, email, permissionLevel, 15min exp), refresh_token (JWT with sub=userId, type='refresh', 7day exp), connection metadata (ip, href, referrer, user_agent). 8) Return tokens and user profile in IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Authenticates a user with email and password credentials on the Economic/Political Discussion Board.

The login operation validates user credentials against the discussion_board_users table. The email must exist in the system and the password must match the stored password_hash. For security, both invalid email and invalid password return the same generic error message to prevent email enumeration attacks.

Banned users cannot log in. If a user's is_banned flag is true, the authentication is rejected with an error message indicating the account has been banned. The ban reason may be displayed to inform the user of the circumstances.

Successful authentication generates a new session record in discussion_board_user_sessions containing: an access_token (JWT valid for 15 minutes with claims: sub, email, permissionLevel), a refresh_token (JWT valid for 7 days for session renewal), and connection metadata (ip address, href, referrer, user_agent) for security auditing.

The response returns the tokens and user profile information including the permission_level (MEMBER, ADMINISTRATOR, or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR), which determines the user's access rights within the platform. The permission level is embedded in the JWT for efficient authorization checks on API calls.

This is a public endpoint - no authentication is required to access it. After successful login, the access token should be included in the Authorization header for all authenticated API requests.

requestBody.description: User login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user profile information for the authenticated user.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implementation: 1) Extract refresh_token from request body. 2) Validate JWT signature and check token hasn't expired (exp claim vs current time). 3) Verify token type is 'refresh' (type claim). 4) Query discussion_board_user_sessions by refresh_token (unique index lookup) to find the session. 5) If session not found or expired_at < now, return AUTH_REFRESH_FAILED error. 6) Query discussion_board_users by session.discussion_board_user_id to get user record. 7) Check user.is_banned - if true, delete session and return AUTH_USER_BANNED error. 8) Generate new access_token with updated claims (sub, email, current permissionLevel, new 15min exp). 9) Update session.access_token with new token. 10) Return new access_token and existing refresh_token in IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Renews an expired access token using a valid refresh token for continued authenticated access.

The refresh operation allows users to obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials when their current access token expires (after 15 minutes). The refresh_token from the original login or previous refresh must be provided in the request body.

The system validates the refresh token by: checking the JWT signature and expiration, verifying the token type is 'refresh', looking up the session record in discussion_board_user_sessions by the refresh_token value, and confirming the session has not expired (expired_at field).

Security checks include verifying the user is not banned (is_banned flag in discussion_board_users). If the user has been banned since the session was created, the session is deleted and authentication is denied.

Upon successful validation, a new access_token is generated with the current permission_level from the user record. This ensures that if a user's permissions were changed (promoted to ADMINISTRATOR or demoted), the new token reflects the current authorization level. The refresh_token remains the same, maintaining the session identity.

The response returns the new access_token and the existing refresh_token. The refresh token's expiration (7 days from original login) is not extended - users must re-authenticate with full login after the refresh token expires.

This is a public endpoint - the refresh token itself serves as the authentication credential for this operation.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile information including display name and biography.

This operation allows users to personalize their profile by modifying their display name (visible to other users alongside their content) and an optional biographical text. The display name serves as the primary identifier shown on articles, comments, and profile pages.

**Display Name Validation:**
- Maximum 50 characters
- Allowed characters: letters (A-Z, a-z), numbers (0-9), spaces, hyphens (-), underscores (_), apostrophes (')
- No consecutive spaces allowed
- No leading or trailing spaces
- Display name uniqueness is NOT required - multiple users may have the same display name

**Bio Validation:**
- Maximum 500 characters
- HTML tags and JavaScript code are not permitted
- Line breaks and basic text formatting are preserved
- The bio field is optional and may be null or empty

**Security Considerations:**
- Users can only update their own profile through the authenticated session
- All input is sanitized to prevent HTML/JavaScript injection
- The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed upon successful update

**Related Operations:**
- GET /profile/at - Retrieve the authenticated user's own profile
- GET /users/{userId} - View another user's profile

This operation updates the discussion_board_users table record associated with the authenticated user.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated user's profile in the discussion_board_users table.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Extract user ID from the authenticated JWT session context
2. Validate request body:
   - display_name: Check length (1-50 chars), character whitelist (alphanumeric, spaces, hyphens, underscores, apostrophes), no consecutive/leading/trailing spaces
   - bio: Check length (<=500 chars), sanitize HTML/JavaScript tags
3. Execute UPDATE query on discussion_board_users:
   - SET display_name = $displayName, bio = $bio, updated_at = NOW()
   - WHERE id = $authenticatedUserId AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. Return the updated user record

**Validation Rules:**
- Display name regex pattern: ^[a-zA-Z0-9\s\-_']+$ after trimming
- No consecutive spaces: check with regex \s{2,}
- Bio sanitization: strip HTML tags, limit to 500 chars

- User not found: Return 404 (account may have been deleted)
- Banned user: Allow profile update (ban status doesn't prevent profile management)
- Empty bio: Accept null or empty string
- Partial update: Only update provided fields (display_name and/or bio)

Each log entry captures the administrator who performed the action, the action type, the target entity affected, the original content author (for content moderation actions), an optional reason, timestamp, and client metadata (IP address, user agent). Logs are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring complete accountability.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering capabilities including action type filtering, target type filtering, administrator identification, date range queries, and full-text search on reason and target title fields.    - Generate UUID for id

operations.description:
Soft deletes a discussion board section, making it and all its content inaccessible to users.

This administrator-only operation marks a section as deleted by setting its deleted_at timestamp. All articles within the section are also soft-deleted, along with their associated comments, file attachments, image attachments, and tag associations becoming hidden from normal browsing.

The operation enforces strict authorization requirements, allowing only users with administrator or super administrator permissions to execute. Non-administrators will receive an authorization error response.

After soft deletion:
- The section and all its articles remain in the database for audit trail preservation
- Content becomes invisible to all users during normal browsing
- Banned users' content visibility rules may still apply
- Physical files remain in storage until cleaned up by an asynchronous process

Business rules enforced:
- Administrator permission required (ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR level)
- Section must exist and not already be deleted
- All articles in the section are soft-deleted (deleted_at set)
- Related content (comments, attachments, tags) remains linked but becomes hidden
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implementation workflow for section deletion:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the authenticated user has ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level. Return 403 Forbidden if insufficient permissions.

2. **Section Lookup**: Query discussion_board_sections table by id (UUID) where deleted_at IS NULL. Return 404 Not Found if section does not exist or is already deleted.

3. **Cascade Article Soft-Delete**: Update all discussion_board_articles records where discussion_board_section_id matches the target section, setting their deleted_at to current timestamp.

4. **Section Soft-Delete**: Set the section's deleted_at to current timestamp.

5. **Response**: Return the soft-deleted section object with id, name, description, creator_id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields.

Transaction scope: All updates must be atomic within a single database transaction to ensure consistency.

Note: Physical file deletion (attachments) may be handled asynchronously by a cleanup process after the transaction completes.

operations.description:
Create a new article in the discussion board.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to create articles within designated sections of the platform. Each article consists of a title, content body, and is assigned to exactly one section. Users can optionally attach files and images, and add free-form tags for categorization.

**Authorization Requirements**:
- User must be authenticated
- User must not be banned

**Validation Rules**:
- Title: 3-200 characters, required
- Content: 10-50,000 characters, required
- Section: must reference an existing section
- Files: maximum 10 files, 10MB each, 50MB total per article
- Images: maximum 20 images, 5MB each, 25MB total per article
- Tags: maximum 15 tags per article, 1-50 characters each, alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores only

**Automatic Fields**:
- Author: set to the authenticated user
- Created At: set to current server time
- Updated At: initially matches Created At

**Related Entities**:
- Files and images are stored and associated with the article
- Tags are normalized to lowercase and associated with the article
- Tag associations are created in the junction table

operations.description:
Update an existing article's content, metadata, and attachments.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify their own articles within the discussion board platform. The operation targets the discussion_board_articles table, updating records identified by their UUID primary key while preserving data integrity through transactional processing.

**Authorization and Security**

Only the article's author can perform updates, verified by matching the authenticated user's ID against discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_user_id. Banned users (discussion_board_users.is_banned = true) cannot edit their articles regardless of ownership. Administrators are explicitly prohibited from editing user articles—this restriction is enforced by the author-only authorization check, as administrators have deletion rights only.

**Editable and Protected Fields**

The operation supports partial updates of the following fields:
- **Title**: Must be 3-200 characters if provided
- **Content**: Must be 10-50,000 characters if provided
- **Section**: Article can be moved to a different section by providing sectionId; referenced section must exist in discussion_board_sections
- **File Attachments**: Add, remove, or replace files (max 10 per article)
- **Image Attachments**: Add, remove, or replace images (max 20 per article)
- **Tags**: Add, remove, or replace tags (max 15 per article)

Non-editable fields that remain protected:
- **Author (discussion_board_user_id)**: Cannot be changed after creation
- **Created At**: Immutable timestamp from article creation
- **Deleted At**: Managed only through delete operations

**Validation and Business Rules**

The article must exist and not be soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). All referenced sections must be active. Tags are normalized to lowercase and validated for allowed characters. File and image attachment limits are enforced per article.

**Related Operations**

- PATCH /discussionBoard/user/articles: Search and list articles with pagination
- GET /discussionBoard/user/articles/{articleId}: Retrieve article details
- DELETE /discussionBoard/user/articles/{articleId}: Delete an article
- GET /discussionBoard/sections: Browse available sections for article assignment

**Response Behavior**

Returns the complete updated article entity with all nested relations (section, author, files, images, tags). The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current server time.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implementation steps for article update:

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify JWT token from Authorization header. Extract user ID from token payload. Return 401 if unauthenticated.

2. **Article Lookup**: Query discussion_board_articles table by articleId. Include relations: files, images, articleTags (with tag). Check deleted_at is null. Return 404 if not found.

3. **Authorization Check**: Compare article.discussion_board_user_id with authenticated user ID. Return 403 if mismatch (NOT_ARTICLE_OWNER). Check user.is_banned is false. Return 403 if banned.

4. **Field Validation** (if provided in request body):
   - title: Validate length 3-200 characters
   - content: Validate length 10-50,000 characters
   - sectionId: Query discussion_board_sections to verify existence and deleted_at is null
   - tags: Validate count <= 15, each tag 1-50 chars, alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores only

5. **Transaction Processing**:
   - Begin database transaction
   - Update article fields (title, content, discussion_board_section_id)
   - Set updated_at to current timestamp
   - Handle file attachments: Process new uploads, delete removed files from storage and DB
   - Handle image attachments: Process new uploads, delete removed images from storage and DB
   - Handle tags: Normalize to lowercase, create new tags if needed, update article_tags junction table
   - Commit transaction

6. **Response**: Query updated article with all relations. Return IDiscussionBoardArticle with populated files, images, and tags arrays.

**Error Codes**:
- AUTH_REQUIRED (401): User not authenticated
- ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND (404): Article doesn't exist or is deleted
- NOT_ARTICLE_OWNER (403): User is not the article author
- USER_BANNED (403): User is banned
- ARTICLE_SECTION_NOT_FOUND (404): Referenced section doesn't exist
- ARTICLE_TITLE_TOO_SHORT/LONG (400): Title validation failed
- ARTICLE_CONTENT_TOO_SHORT/LONG (400): Content validation failed

Permanently removes an article from the discussion board along with all its associated content.

This operation performs a hard delete that completely removes the article record from the database. Article authors can delete their own articles, and administrators can delete any article. When an article is permanently deleted, the system performs cascade deletion of all related entities including comments, file attachments, image attachments, and tag associations.

Authorization requires the requesting user to be either the article's author or an administrator. Banned users are denied deletion access regardless of ownership.

Warning: This action is irreversible. Deleted articles cannot be recovered. For content moderation that preserves data for audit purposes, administrators should use moderation tools that preserve records.

The discussion_board_articles table stores articles with id (UUID), title, content, section reference, author reference, and timestamps.

   - Delete all discussion_board_comments records where discussion_board_article_id matches
   - Delete physical files from storage for discussion_board_article_files records
   - Delete discussion_board_article_files records

- Return 403 if user lacks permission (not author and not admin)
- Return 403 if user is banned (when author)
- Return 404 if article does not exist

operations.description:
Manage file attachments for a specific article by adding new files or removing existing ones.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to modify the file attachments on their articles. Users can upload new files to attach to the article and remove existing attachments by specifying their IDs. The operation supports partial updates - only specify the files to add or remove.

Authorization is strictly limited to the article's author. Any attempt by a non-author to modify attachments will result in a 403 Forbidden error. Additionally, users who have been banned from the platform cannot modify their articles' attachments even if they are the original author.

File attachments are subject to comprehensive validation:

- **File Count**: Maximum 10 file attachments per article. Attempts to exceed this limit will return a validation error.
- **Individual File Size**: Maximum 10MB per file. Files exceeding this limit will be rejected.
- **Total Attachment Size**: Maximum 50MB combined size for all file attachments on the article.
- **Allowed File Types**: Only specific document and archive formats are permitted:
  - Documents: PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, RTF
  - Spreadsheets: XLS, XLSX, CSV
  - Presentations: PPT, PPTX
  - Archives: ZIP, RAR, 7Z

When files are removed, the physical files are permanently deleted from storage and their database records are cascade deleted. The original_filename is preserved for display and download purposes while a system-generated unique filename is used for storage to prevent conflicts.

Related operations:
- Use GET /articles/{articleId} to view article details with all attachments
- Use PATCH /articles/{articleId}/images to manage image attachments separately
operations.name: updateFiles
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify JWT token validity. Return 401 with AUTH_REQUIRED if not authenticated.

2. **Article Validation**: Query discussion_board_articles table for the specified articleId. Return 404 with ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND if article doesn't exist.

3. **Authorization Check**: Compare discussion_board_user_id of the article with authenticated user's ID. Return 403 with NOT_ARTICLE_OWNER if mismatch.

4. **Ban Status Check**: Query discussion_board_users to check if user has an active ban (is_banned = true). Return 403 with USER_BANNED if banned.

5. **Process Removals**: For each fileId in removals array:
   - Verify file belongs to the article (discussion_board_article_id matches)
   - Delete physical file from storage using storage_path
   - Delete record from discussion_board_article_files (cascade on delete handles this)

6. **Process Additions**: For each file in additions array:
   - Validate file type against allowed MIME types (check mime_type field)
   - Validate file size <= 10MB (10,485,760 bytes)
   - Calculate new total size and verify <= 50MB
   - Count current + new files and verify <= 10 total
   - Generate unique storage_path (UUID-based filename)
   - Store file in object storage
   - Insert record into discussion_board_article_files with:
     - discussion_board_article_id: the article's ID
     - original_filename: user-provided filename
     - storage_path: generated unique path
     - file_size: in bytes
     - mime_type: validated MIME type
     - created_at: current timestamp

7. **Return Response**: Query all files for the article and return as array of file summaries (id, original_filename, file_size, mime_type, created_at). Exclude storage_path from response.

Error handling:
- FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED: MIME type not in allowed list
- FILE_SIZE_EXCEEDED: File > 10MB
- FILE_COUNT_EXCEEDED: Total files would exceed 10
- ARTICLE_ATTACHMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Total size would exceed 50MB
- FILE_NOT_FOUND: Specified removal fileId doesn't exist or doesn't belong to article

operations.description:
Update the set of tags associated with a specific article.

This operation allows authenticated users to replace all tags on their own articles. Tags provide flexible, user-defined categorization beyond section-based organization. The operation validates each tag value, normalizes them to lowercase, removes duplicates, and updates the article-tag associations.

**Authorization**: Only the article author can update tags. Banned users are denied access regardless of ownership. Administrators cannot edit user article tags (only deletion rights are granted to administrators).

**Validation Rules**:
- Maximum 15 tags per article
- Each tag must be 1-50 characters
- Tags can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), and underscores (_)
- Tags are normalized to lowercase before storage
- Duplicate tags (after normalization) are automatically removed

**Process**:
1. Verify article exists and user is the author
2. Validate each tag in the request
3. Normalize tags to lowercase and remove duplicates
4. For each tag, create or reference existing tag in discussion_board_tags
5. Remove existing article-tag associations
6. Create new article-tag associations in discussion_board_article_tags

**Database References**:
- discussion_board_articles.id - the target article
- discussion_board_tags - master tag registry (tags are reused platform-wide)
- discussion_board_article_tags - junction table for article-tag relationships

Implementation requires transaction-based tag replacement workflow:

1. **Authentication & Authorization Check**:
   - Extract user ID from JWT token
   - Query discussion_board_articles to verify articleId exists
   - Verify discussion_board_user_id matches authenticated user ID
   - Check user is not banned (via discussion_board_users.permission_level or discussion_board_bans)

2. **Tag Validation & Normalization**:
   - Validate array length <= 15
   - For each tag string:
     - Trim whitespace
     - Validate length 1-50 characters
     - Validate regex pattern: ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ (alphanumeric, hyphen, underscore only)
     - Convert to lowercase for normalization
   - Remove duplicate values after normalization

3. **Transaction-Based Update**:
   - Begin database transaction
   - For each normalized tag value:
     - INSERT INTO discussion_board_tags (id, value, created_at, updated_at) if not exists (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
     - Retrieve tag ID (existing or newly created)
   - DELETE FROM discussion_board_article_tags WHERE discussion_board_article_id = :articleId
   - For each tag:
     - INSERT INTO discussion_board_article_tags (id, discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_tag_id, created_at)
   - Commit transaction

4. **Response Construction**:
   - Query updated tags for the article
   - Return paginated format with all associated tags

operations.description:
Create a new comment on an article.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to post comments on articles within the discussion board. Comments are stored in the `discussion_board_comments` table as single-level attachments to articles, supporting direct discussions without nested replies. Each comment references the parent `discussion_board_articles` record via `discussion_board_article_id` and the author's `discussion_board_users` record via `discussion_board_user_id`.

The comment `content` field must contain meaningful text between 1 and 10,000 characters after whitespace trimming, as defined in the comment system requirements. The system automatically generates a sequential `citizen_id` from `discussion_board_comment_citizens` for human-readable identification.

Authentication is required for this operation. Unauthenticated requests will be rejected with an authentication error. Banned users (where `is_banned` is true in `discussion_board_users`) are prohibited from creating comments and will receive a 403 Forbidden error with code `ACCOUNT_BANNED`.

The target article must exist and not be soft-deleted (`deleted_at` is null). If the specified articleId does not correspond to an existing article, the operation will fail with a 404 Not Found error.

Upon successful creation, the comment is immediately visible in the article's comment section, sorted chronologically by `created_at` with oldest comments first. The response includes the newly generated comment with its unique `id`, sequential `citizen_id`, and creation timestamp.

1. **Authentication Validation**: Verify the request includes valid authentication credentials. Extract the authenticated user's ID from the JWT token.

2. **Ban Status Check**: Query discussion_board_users table to verify the authenticated user is not currently banned (check for active ban records in discussion_board_bans where user_id matches and unban does not exist). Return 403 Forbidden if banned.

3. **Article Existence Check**: Query discussion_board_articles table to verify the articleId exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Return 404 Not Found if article does not exist.

4. **Content Validation**: Validate comment content meets requirements:
   - Trim leading/trailing whitespace
   - Ensure at least 1 non-whitespace character remains
   - Ensure content does not exceed 10,000 characters
   - Return 400 Bad Request with validation errors if constraints violated

5. **Citizen ID Generation**: Create a new record in discussion_board_comment_citizens table to obtain a sequential citizen_id for human-readable comment identification.

6. **Comment Creation**: Insert new record into discussion_board_comments table with:
   - id: Generate new UUID
   - citizen_id: UUID from step 5
   - discussion_board_article_id: From path parameter
   - discussion_board_user_id: From authenticated user context
   - content: Trimmed comment text
   - created_at: Current timestamp
   - updated_at: null (never edited)
   - deleted_at: null (active comment)

7. **Response**: Return the created comment entity with all fields populated.

operations.description:
Soft deletes a comment from an article's discussion thread.

This operation allows authorized users to delete comments from articles. There are two types of authorized deletors: the comment author who wishes to remove their own comment, and administrators performing content moderation. When a comment is deleted, the system marks it as deleted via the deleted_at timestamp field rather than permanently removing the record from the database.

The soft delete approach preserves the comment record for audit purposes while excluding it from public display. Once deleted, the comment content is no longer visible to any user, including administrators. The article's comment count is automatically updated to reflect the deletion.

Authorization is enforced by verifying that the authenticated user is either the comment author (matching discussion_board_user_id) or holds administrator privileges (permission_level of ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR). Users who are neither the comment author nor administrators will receive a 403 Forbidden error.

The operation validates that both the article (discussion_board_articles.id) and comment (discussion_board_comments.id) exist and are not already deleted. If the article has been soft-deleted, attempting to delete its comments will result in a 404 Not Found error. Similarly, attempting to delete an already-deleted comment returns a 404 Not Found error.

3. **Article Existence Check**: Query discussion_board_articles table to verify the article exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). Return 404 if article not found or deleted.

4. **Comment Existence Check**: Query discussion_board_comments table to verify:
   - The comment exists (id = commentId)
   - The comment belongs to the specified article (discussion_board_article_id = articleId)
   - The comment is not already deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   Return 404 if comment not found, doesn't belong to the article, or is already deleted.

5. **Authorization Check**: Verify the authenticated user has permission to delete:
   - Option A: User is the comment author (discussion_board_user_id matches authenticated user's ID)
   - Option B: User has administrator privileges (permission_level = 'ADMINISTRATOR' or 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR')
   Return 403 Forbidden if neither condition is met.

6. **Soft Delete Execution**: Update the comment record:
   - Set deleted_at to current timestamp
   - Do NOT modify updated_at (that field tracks content edits, not deletions)

7. **Comment Count Update**: Decrement the article's comment count in any cached/aggregated storage (if applicable). This may be handled by a database trigger or application logic.

8. **Response**: Return 204 No Content (null response body) on successful deletion.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid JWT token
- 403 Forbidden: User is not comment author and not an administrator
- 404 Not Found: Article or comment not found, or comment already deleted
- 500 Internal Server Error: Database or system errors

operations.description:
Ban a user from the platform, preventing them from logging in while preserving their existing content.

This operation allows administrators to restrict platform access for users who violate community guidelines or terms of service. When a user is banned, they cannot log in to the platform, but their existing articles and comments remain visible to other users to maintain discussion continuity.
The operation enforces strict authorization rules based on the administrative hierarchy:
- Regular administrators can ban regular users but cannot ban other administrators or super administrators
- Super administrators can ban regular users and regular administrators
- Super administrators can ban other super administrators
- No administrator can ban themselves

The ban reason must be between 10 and 1000 characters and is recorded for transparency, audit purposes, and potential appeals processes. All ban records in the discussion_board_bans table are immutable and persist indefinitely for compliance and administrative oversight, even after unbanning.

Upon successful ban execution, the system immediately terminates all active sessions for the banned user from the discussion_board_user_sessions table, ensuring they cannot continue using authenticated features. The user's is_banned flag in discussion_board_users is updated to reflect the banned state.

This operation may fail with the following error conditions:
- BAN_SELF_PROHIBITED (400): Administrator attempting to ban themselves
- BAN_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION (403): Administrator lacks permission to ban target user
- USER_ALREADY_BANNED (400): Target user is already banned
- BAN_REASON_REQUIRED (400): Ban reason not provided
- BAN_REASON_TOO_SHORT (400): Ban reason is less than 10 characters
- BAN_REASON_TOO_LONG (400): Ban reason exceeds 1,000 characters
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation steps for ban creation:

1. **Authorization Validation**:
   - Extract administrator ID from authenticated session
   - Verify the authenticated user has ADMINISTRATOR or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level
   - Return 401 if not authenticated, 403 if not an administrator

2. **Self-Ban Prevention**:
   - Compare target user ID with administrator's own user ID
   - If equal, return error with code BAN_SELF_PROHIBITED (400)

3. **Permission Hierarchy Check**:
   - Query discussion_board_users to get target user's permission_level
   - Compare administrator's permission level with target's:
     - MEMBER < ADMINISTRATOR < SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR
   - If target has equal or higher permission, return error with code BAN_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION (403)

4. **Already-Banned Check**:
   - Check if target user's is_banned field is true
   - If already banned, return error with code USER_ALREADY_BANNED (400)

5. **Reason Validation**:
   - Verify reason is provided and not empty
   - If missing, return error with code BAN_REASON_REQUIRED (400)
   - If length > 1000 characters, return error with code BAN_REASON_TOO_LONG (400)

6. **Ban Record Creation**:
   - Generate UUID for new ban record
   - Insert record into discussion_board_bans with:
     - id: generated UUID
     - discussion_board_user_id: target user ID from request
     - discussion_board_administrator_id: administrator's user ID from session
     - reason: validated reason text
     - created_at: current timestamp

7. **User Status Update**:
   - Update discussion_board_users record for target user:
     - Set is_banned = true
     - Set banned_by = administrator's user ID
     - Set updated_at = current timestamp

8. **Session Invalidation**:
   - Query discussion_board_user_sessions for all sessions belonging to target user
   - Delete all found session records (or mark as invalidated)

9. **Response**:
   - Return the created ban record with full details including administrator info and timestamp

operations.description:
Search for articles across all sections by matching text in the title or content fields of the discussion_board_articles table.

This operation provides full-text search capabilities across the entire discussion board, enabling users to discover articles containing specific keywords or phrases. The search scans both article titles and content bodies for matches, returning a paginated list of matching articles with summary information.

Results can be filtered by one or more tags using OR logic - articles matching ANY of the specified tags will be included in results. Tag filtering is implemented through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table, which links articles to entries in the discussion_board_tags master table. When combining search query with tag filters, articles must match the search text AND have at least one of the specified tags.

The search requires a minimum of 2 characters in the query string to prevent overly broad results. Results are sorted by the created_at timestamp from discussion_board_articles, either newest first (default) or oldest first, and are paginated with a maximum of 20 articles per page.

Each result entry includes the article title, author display name from discussion_board_users, associated tags from discussion_board_tags, comment count from discussion_board_comments (excluding soft-deleted comments), and posting timestamp. Clicking on a result navigates to the full article detail view. Empty results display an appropriate message with suggestions for refining the search query.

Public access is granted to all users including guests, allowing content discovery without authentication requirements. The operation respects soft-deletion status by excluding articles where the deleted_at field is set.

operations.specification:
Implement full-text search on discussion_board_articles table using PostgreSQL full-text search capabilities on title and content columns.

Query construction:
1. Filter articles where deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted content
2. Apply full-text search using PostgreSQL tsvector on title and content
3. If tag filters provided, join discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags to filter by tag values (OR logic)
4. Apply sorting by created_at (DESC for newest, ASC for oldest)
5. Apply pagination using LIMIT/OFFSET based on request parameters

Database queries:
- Use LEFT JOIN with discussion_board_users for author display_name
- Use LEFT JOIN with discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags for tag aggregation
- Use subquery to count comments per article from discussion_board_comments where deleted_at IS NULL

Performance considerations:
- Add GIN index on title column for trigram search (already exists per schema)
- Consider caching popular search queries
- Return results within 2 seconds as per non-functional requirements

Validation:
- Minimum query length: 2 characters (return validation error if shorter)
- Maximum page size: 20 items
- Default sort: newest first (created_at DESC)

operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator request, granting the requester regular administrator status.

This operation allows super administrators to review and approve administrator requests submitted by users seeking administrative privileges. Upon approval, the requester's account is updated from MEMBER to ADMINISTRATOR permission level, enabling them to perform moderation tasks, manage sections, and ban users.

The approval process updates the admin request record by setting the status to 'approved', recording the reviewer's identity, capturing the reviewed_at timestamp, and storing any optional review notes. An audit log entry is created in discussion_board_admin_action_logs with action_type APPROVE_REQUEST to maintain accountability.

This operation enforces authorization constraints: only users with SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level may approve requests. The target request must exist and have a status of 'pending'. Attempting to approve a request that has already been approved or rejected will result in an error. Super administrators cannot approve their own requests as they are already administrators.

Related operations: GET /adminRequests (list pending requests), POST /adminRequests/{adminRequestId}/reject (reject request).
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. Authenticate and verify the current user has SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission level
2. Validate the adminRequestId parameter (must be valid UUID)
3. Query discussion_board_admin_requests table to find the target request by id
4. Verify the request exists and has status 'pending'
5. Verify the requester is not the current user (self-approval prevention)
6. Verify the requester is not already an administrator
7. Create a database transaction:
   a. Update discussion_board_admin_requests: set status='approved', reviewer_id=current_user.id, reviewed_at=now(), review_notes=provided_notes, updated_at=now()
   b. Update discussion_board_users: set permission_level='ADMINISTRATOR' where id=request.requester_id
   c. Create discussion_board_admin_action_logs entry: administrator_id=current_user.id, original_author_id=request.requester_id, action_type='APPROVE_REQUEST', target_type='ADMIN_REQUEST', target_id=request.id, target_title=requester.display_name, reason=review_notes, ip=request.ip, user_agent=request.user_agent, created_at=now()
8. Commit the transaction
9. Return the updated admin request with populated requester and reviewer relations

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not a super administrator
- 404 Not Found: Admin request not found
- 409 Conflict: Request already processed (not pending)
- 409 Conflict: Requester is already an administrator
- 409 Conflict: Self-approval attempt

The operation is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators and regular users cannot access this endpoint. The admin request must exist and be in 'pending' status to be rejected. Attempting to reject an already processed (approved or rejected) request will result in an error.

This operation is part of the administrator management workflow, which includes viewing pending requests, approving requests, and managing the admin hierarchy. Each rejection is logged in the admin action logs for audit purposes.

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator status.

This operation allows super administrators to elevate regular administrators to the highest permission level in the platform hierarchy. Upon successful promotion, the target user gains all super administrator privileges including the ability to review and approve administrator requests, and to promote or demote other administrators.

The promotion process includes several validation steps: the caller must be a super administrator, the target user must currently be a regular administrator (not a regular member or already a super administrator), and the target user must not be banned. If any of these conditions are not met, the operation will fail with an appropriate error message.

All promotion actions are recorded in the audit trail (discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions table) with the actor's identity, target's identity, action type 'PROMOTION', optional reason, and timestamp. This ensures accountability and enables historical tracking of all hierarchy changes.

Related operations: Use POST /administrators/{administratorId}/demote to reverse this action (demote a super administrator to regular administrator). Use PATCH /administrators to list administrators and their current permission levels.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification:
Implement promotion workflow:

1. Authentication & Authorization:
   - Verify caller is authenticated
   - Verify caller has SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission_level
   - Return 403 Forbidden if caller is not a super administrator

2. Target Validation:
   - Query discussion_board_users by administratorId path parameter
   - Return 404 Not Found if user does not exist
   - Verify target's permission_level is 'ADMINISTRATOR' (not MEMBER or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR)
   - Return 400 Bad Request if target is not a regular administrator
   - Verify target's is_banned is false
   - Return 400 Bad Request if target is banned

3. Self-Promotion Prevention:
   - Verify administratorId does not match caller's user ID
   - Return 400 Bad Request if attempting self-promotion

4. Execute Promotion:
   - Update target user's permission_level to 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR'
   - Update target user's updated_at timestamp

5. Create Audit Record:
   - Insert record into discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions:
     - actor_id: caller's user ID
     - target_id: administratorId
     - action_type: 'PROMOTION'
     - reason: optional reason from request body (or null)
     - created_at: current timestamp

6. Return Response:
   - Return updated user object with new permission level

7. Send Notification:
   - Trigger notification to promoted user about their elevation

operations.description:
Demotes a super administrator to regular administrator status.

This operation allows a super administrator to downgrade another super administrator's permission level from SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR to ADMINISTRATOR. The demotion is recorded in the admin hierarchy audit trail for compliance purposes.

**Authorization Requirements**: Only super administrators can perform this operation.

**Business Rules**:
- The target user must currently be a super administrator
- A super administrator cannot demote themselves (self-protection mechanism)
- At least one super administrator must remain in the system after demotion
- The demotion takes effect immediately upon successful execution

**Audit Trail**: The operation creates an immutable record in the admin_hierarchy_actions table containing the actor's ID, target's ID, action type 'DEMOTION', optional reason, and timestamp.

**Related Operations**: After demotion, the affected user retains regular administrator privileges. To restore super administrator status, use the promote operation (POST /administrators/{administratorId}/promote).
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the authenticated user has SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR permission_level in discussion_board_users table.

2. **Target Validation**:
   - Query discussion_board_users to find the target administrator by administratorId
   - Verify target exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   - Verify target's permission_level equals 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR'
   - Verify target's id does not match the actor's id (prevent self-demotion)

3. **Last Super Admin Check**:
   - Count users with permission_level = 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR' and is_banned = false and deleted_at IS NULL
   - If count would be zero after demotion, reject with appropriate error

4. **Execute Demotion**:
   - Update target's permission_level to 'ADMINISTRATOR' in discussion_board_users
   - Update target's updated_at timestamp

5. **Create Audit Record**:
   - Insert record into discussion_board_admin_hierarchy_actions with:
     - actor_id: current authenticated user's id
     - target_id: the demoted administrator's id
     - action_type: 'DEMOTION'
     - reason: from request body (may be null)
     - created_at: current timestamp

6. **Return Response**: Return the updated user object with new ADMINISTRATOR permission level.

**Error Handling**:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not a super administrator
- 404 Not Found: Target administrator does not exist
- 400 Bad Request: Target is not a super administrator
- 400 Bad Request: Self-demotion attempt
- 400 Bad Request: Would result in zero super administrators

responseBody.description: The demoted administrator with updated permission level

If the user is currently banned, the operation retrieves the most recent active ban record from the discussion_board_bans table, which contains the reason (10-1000 characters), the administrator reference who performed the ban, and the creation timestamp.

This endpoint supports the administrative workflow for user management, enabling administrators to quickly verify ban status before taking further moderation actions or responding to user inquiries.

Implementation: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL always applied. search: ILIKE pattern match on discussion_board_articles.title OR discussion_board_articles.content columns. sectionId: exact match filter on discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_section_id foreign key. tags: JOIN through discussion_board_article_tags junction to discussion_board_tags, filter by tag value with OR logic. sort: ORDER BY created_at DESC (newest) or ASC (oldest). page: OFFSET = (page-1)*limit. limit: LIMIT clause with max 100. Defaults: page=1, limit=20, sort=newest. Minimum search length: 2 characters for performance.

displayName.description: Search text for filtering users by display name. Supports partial matching - users with names containing the provided text will be included in results.
displayName.x-autobe-specification: Case-insensitive partial match filter referencing discussion_board_users.display_name column. Uses GIN trigram index (gin_trgm_ops) for efficient fuzzy text search. Query: WHERE display_name ILIKE '%{displayName}%'

email.description: Search text for filtering users by email address. Supports partial matching for finding users with email addresses containing the provided text.
email.x-autobe-specification: Case-insensitive partial match filter referencing discussion_board_users.email column. Query: WHERE email ILIKE '%{email}%'

permissionLevel.description: Filter users by permission level. Valid values: MEMBER (regular user), ADMINISTRATOR, or SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR. This filter is restricted to administrators only.
permissionLevel.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter referencing discussion_board_users.permission_level column. Valid values: 'MEMBER', 'ADMINISTRATOR', 'SUPER_ADMINISTRATOR'. Query: WHERE permission_level = {permissionLevel}. Admin-only filter - regular users receive error when using this parameter.

isBanned.description: Filter users by ban status. Set to true to see only banned users, false to see only active users. This filter is restricted to administrators only.
isBanned.x-autobe-specification: Boolean filter referencing discussion_board_users.is_banned column. true = only banned users, false = only active users. Query: WHERE is_banned = {isBanned}. Admin-only filter - regular users receive error when using this parameter.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts at 1 for the first page. Use with limit to navigate through result pages.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for pagination. Controls OFFSET calculation: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Default: 1. Must be >= 1. Combined with limit to determine result window.

limit.description: Maximum number of user profiles to return per page. Default is 20, maximum is 100. Use with page for pagination control.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page. Controls LIMIT clause in query. Default: 20. Maximum: 100. Must be >= 1 and <= 100. Combined with page to determine result window.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IRequest.description: Search and filter parameters for retrieving a paginated list of user profiles. Supports partial text matching on display name and email, filtering by permission level and ban status, and standard pagination controls. All parameters are optional and can be combined for refined searches.
IDiscussionBoardUser.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for searching and filtering user profiles. Properties serve as query parameters for WHERE clause construction and OFFSET/LIMIT pagination against discussion_board_users table. Filter parameters reference DB columns: displayName→display_name (ILIKE), email→email (ILIKE), permissionLevel→permission_level (exact), isBanned→is_banned (exact). Pagination parameters (page, limit) control result windowing. All parameters optional. Used by PATCH /discussionBoard/users endpoint.

id.description: Unique identifier for the unban record.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans.id. Auto-generated UUID primary key.

ban.description: The original ban record that this unban action reverses.
ban.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via discussion_board_ban_id foreign key to discussion_board_bans.id. Returns full IDiscussionBoardBan entity containing the original ban record details including the banned user, ban reason, and the administrator who performed the ban.

administrator.description: The administrator who performed the unban action.
administrator.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via administrator_id foreign key to discussion_board_users.id. Returns IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary containing id, displayName, and email of the administrator who performed the unban action.

reason.description: The documented reason for lifting the ban, recorded for transparency and audit purposes.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans.reason. Text field validated to be between 10 and 1000 characters. Records the administrative justification for reversing the ban.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the unban action was recorded.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp of when the unban action was performed.

IDiscussionBoardUnban.description: Unban record representing the reversal of an active user ban. Contains the original ban record being reversed, the administrator who performed the unban action, the documented reason for the reversal, and the creation timestamp. Unban records maintain a complete audit trail of ban removal decisions for administrative accountability and compliance purposes.
IDiscussionBoardUnban.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_unbans table. Primary key: id (UUID). Columns: reason (text, validated 10-1000 chars), created_at (timestamp). Relations: ban (JOIN via discussion_board_ban_id FK to discussion_board_bans.id, returns IDiscussionBoardBan entity), administrator (JOIN via administrator_id FK to discussion_board_users.id, returns IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary). Raw FK columns (discussion_board_ban_id, administrator_id) excluded in favor of nested objects. Soft-delete and update tracking columns (deleted_at, updated_at) excluded as internal fields.

value.description: Tag value to associate with the article. The value will be normalized to lowercase and matched to an existing platform tag or used to create a new one automatically. Supports alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores only.
value.x-autobe-specification: User-provided tag text input. Processing pipeline: 1) Trim leading/trailing whitespace, 2) Validate length (1-50 characters), 3) Validate characters (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores only), 4) Normalize to lowercase for case-insensitive comparison, 5) Lookup in discussion_board_tags table by unique value constraint, 6) Create new tag record in discussion_board_tags if not found, 7) Create association in discussion_board_article_tags linking article to tag. Does not map directly to any discussion_board_article_tags column.

IDiscussionBoardArticleTag.ICreate.description: Request body for adding tags to an article. Contains the tag value to associate with the article. The tag value is automatically normalized to lowercase and will reference an existing platform tag or create a new one automatically.
IDiscussionBoardArticleTag.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Transformation DTO for article-tag association. The value field receives user-provided tag text, which is normalized (trimmed, lowercased), validated (1-50 characters, alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores only), then used to lookup or create a record in discussion_board_tags. The resulting tag ID is linked to the article via discussion_board_article_tags junction table. Article ID is sourced from the path parameter {articleId}, not the request body. Maximum 15 tags per article enforced at application layer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.id. UUID format generated by database.

displayName.description: User's display name shown on their profile and alongside their content. Visible to other users.
displayName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.display_name. Transform snake_case to camelCase.

email.description: User's primary email address used for authentication.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users.email. Used for authentication and identification.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.description: Lightweight user profile summary for display in lists, article authors, comment authors, and administrative records. Contains essential identification (id, email) and display name without exposing sensitive data or detailed activity information. Used across public contexts (viewing article/comment authors) and administrative contexts (ban records, admin action audit trails, request workflows).
IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_users table for summary display. Query columns: id, display_name, email. Transform snake_case to camelCase: display_name → displayName. Exclude sensitive field password_hash and detailed profile fields. This summary is used for user display in article authors, comment authors, admin action logs, ban records, admin request requesters/reviewers, session user references, and hierarchy action actors/targets. No JOINs required for ISummary fields.

IDiscussionBoardBanHistory.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary of a ban or unban action record for audit trail list display. Captures essential information for administrative review: the action type, target user, administrator who performed the action, reason for transparency, and timestamp.
IDiscussionBoardBanHistory.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_ban_histories table with relation joins for user summaries. Query selects: id, action_type, reason, created_at from discussion_board_ban_histories. Joins discussion_board_users twice via discussion_board_user_id and actor_id to populate targetUser and actor summaries. Both user references may be null in database (for deleted users per FR-AUDIT-005) but returned as nullable ISummary in response. Sort order is handled by parent query.

reviewNotes.description: Optional notes from the super administrator explaining the approval decision. Provides context for audit trails and administrative transparency.
reviewNotes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to discussion_board_admin_requests.review_notes column. Optional text field allowing the super administrator to document the rationale for approving the request. Stored as nullable VARCHAR in database. If null, the approval proceeds without explanatory notes.

IDiscussionBoardAdminRequest.IApprove.description: Request body for approving a pending administrator request. Contains optional review notes from the super administrator explaining the approval decision. The administrator request ID is provided in the URL path, and the reviewer's identity is automatically obtained from the authentication token.
IDiscussionBoardAdminRequest.IApprove.x-autobe-specification: Request body for the admin request approval operation. The reviewNotes field maps directly to the review_notes column in discussion_board_admin_requests table. Upon approval, the system automatically sets: status='approved', reviewer_id from JWT authentication context, reviewed_at to current timestamp, updated_at to current timestamp. The id is provided via path parameter, and requester_id/reason are preserved from the existing request record. The reviewer relation is populated from the authenticated super administrator's user record.

limit.description: Maximum number of comments to return per page. Accepts values from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20 when not specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter controlling maximum records per page. Maps to SQL LIMIT clause. Value range: 1-100 (enforced by minimum/maximum constraints). Used in OFFSET calculation: LIMIT = limit. Default: 20 when null. Capped at 100 to prevent excessive result sets.

page.description: Page number to retrieve, starting from 1. Defaults to 1 when not specified. Use together with limit to navigate through results.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter for page navigation. 1-indexed page number used to calculate SQL OFFSET: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Default: 1 (first page) when null. Minimum: 1. Used together with limit for standard pagination pattern.

search.description: Search term to filter comments by their content. Performs case-insensitive partial match. Leave empty or null to skip content filtering.
search.x-autobe-specification: Search parameter for filtering comments by content. When provided, performs case-insensitive LIKE query: WHERE content ILIKE '%search%'. Searches discussion_board_comments.content column for partial matches. Null means no content filter applied. Trimming recommended before query execution.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description: Request parameters for retrieving a paginated list of comments on an article. Supports searching within comment content and standard pagination controls. All parameters are optional - omit to use default pagination settings.
IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request DTO for comment list pagination and search. Used as query parameters in PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments endpoint. Properties control pagination (limit, page) and content filtering (search). The article context comes from path parameter {articleId}, not request body. Implementation: page and limit compute OFFSET and LIMIT for SQL query; search performs case-insensitive LIKE query on discussion_board_comments.content column when provided. All fields optional with sensible defaults (page=1, limit=20, search=null).

isBanned.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the user is currently banned from the platform. When true, the user cannot log in or access platform features, but their existing content remains visible.
isBanned.x-autobe-specification: Derived from discussion_board_users.is_banned column via primary query. Query: SELECT is_banned FROM discussion_board_users WHERE id = userId (path parameter). Returns boolean indicating current ban status. When true, the user cannot authenticate or access the platform. This column is the authoritative source for ban status in the system.

ban.description: Ban record details when the user is currently banned, or null if the user is not banned. When present, contains the ban reason, administrator who performed the action, and timestamp for administrative transparency.
ban.x-autobe-specification: Computed property populated via secondary query when isBanned is true. Query: SELECT b.id, b.reason, b.created_at FROM discussion_board_bans b WHERE b.discussion_board_user_id = userId ORDER BY b.created_at DESC LIMIT 1. Includes JOIN to discussion_board_users for administrator details via discussion_board_administrator_id. Returns IDiscussionBoardBan.ISummary containing id, reason, created_at, user (banned user), and administrator (who performed the ban). Administrator is nullable if admin account was soft-deleted. Returns null when user is not banned.

IDiscussionBoardBanStatus.description: Response object representing a user's current ban status. Contains a boolean flag indicating whether the user is currently banned from the platform. When the user is banned, includes the complete ban record with reason, the administrator who performed the ban action, and the timestamp. When the user is not banned, the ban field is null. Used by administrators to verify user moderation status before taking further actions.
IDiscussionBoardBanStatus.x-autobe-specification: Computed response type aggregating ban status from two database sources. Primary query: SELECT is_banned FROM discussion_board_users WHERE id = userId. If is_banned = true, secondary query: SELECT b.id, b.reason, b.created_at, u.display_name, u.email, a.display_name, a.email FROM discussion_board_bans b JOIN discussion_board_users u ON b.discussion_board_user_id = u.id LEFT JOIN discussion_board_users a ON b.discussion_board_administrator_id = a.id WHERE b.discussion_board_user_id = userId ORDER BY b.created_at DESC LIMIT 1. Returns: isBanned (boolean from users.is_banned), ban (IDiscussionBoardBan.ISummary or null). Administrator may be null if the admin account was soft-deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the file attachment.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.id. UUID primary key auto-generated on file creation. Used to uniquely identify the file attachment for retrieval and download operations.

original_filename.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user, preserved for display and download.
original_filename.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.original_filename. Preserves the user's uploaded filename for display and download purposes. Maximum 255 characters. Used as the download filename header.

storage_path.description: Server-side storage path for file retrieval.
storage_path.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.storage_path. Server-side file location path used internally for file retrieval operations. Not exposed to end users in download URLs.

file_size.description: File size in bytes, used for quota enforcement.
file_size.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.file_size. Integer value in bytes for quota tracking and validation. Individual files limited to 10MB (10,485,760 bytes). Used for total article quota enforcement (50MB max).

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file, used for download content-type headers and validation.
mime_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.mime_type. MIME type string validated against allowed document formats (PDF, DOC/DOCX, TXT, RTF, XLS/XLSX, CSV, PPT/PPTX, ZIP/RAR/7Z). Used for Content-Type header during file download.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from discussion_board_article_files.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp automatically set on file creation. Used for chronological ordering of attachments and audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.description: File attachment metadata for discussion board articles. Contains original filename preserved for display and download, storage location for file retrieval, file size for quota tracking, and MIME type for validation and download headers. Supports document formats including PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and archive files.
IDiscussionBoardArticleFile.x-autobe-specification: Read DTO mapping from discussion_board_article_files table. All scalar columns exposed directly: id (UUID primary key, auto-generated), original_filename (preserved from user upload, max 255 chars for display/download), storage_path (server-side file location for retrieval operations), file_size (integer bytes for quota validation, max 10MB per file), mime_type (validated against allowed document types for content-type headers), created_at (upload timestamp, auto-set). FK column discussion_board_article_id excluded - resolved from path parameter {articleId} in parent operation context. Article relation excluded - prevents circular dependency; parent article accessible via separate endpoint. Files cascade deleted when parent article is removed.
